sections.title: The first workshop
paragraphs: The crafting table expands the small inventory grid into a 3 × 3 workspace. Place it on a block, use it, choose a recipe, then collect the output. It is the station for recipes too large for the inventory grid; opening the interface alone does not supply any missing ingredients.

sections.title: Four planks, one table
paragraphs: Convert a log into planks, then put four planks into the four inventory crafting slots. Collect the table before closing the screen. The official illustrated guide shows each step, so a new player can compare the actual interface rather than trying to identify the recipe from an isolated item icon.

sections.title: Recipe book and ingredient checks
paragraphs: The recipe book groups recipes and supports searching. Selecting a recipe helps arrange its ingredients; missing supplies are highlighted. If the output is empty, check both the material and its position. A useful practice sequence is to make sticks, then a wooden pickaxe, and keep the table nearby while preparing your first stone tools.

sections.title: Edition and identifier
paragraphs: This entry belongs to the Java 26.1 data snapshot. Its catalog number 333 is a provider record, not a universal command ID. The named identifier is minecraft:crafting_table. Bedrock also has crafting tables, but its menus, numeric data and older achievement history must be read separately. Resource packs can change the table texture without changing its purpose.

history.label: An evolving interface
history.detail: The community history records Bedrock recipe-book support in 1.2.0 and a texture update in 1.10.0. These are historical milestones, not claims that this catalog is running those versions.

sections.title: Build a basic furnace
paragraphs: Arrange eight cobblestone around the outside of the crafting table grid, leaving the center empty. Collect the furnace, place it beside your work area and open it with the use action. This is a practical first smelting setup: keep the crafting table close enough that you can turn processed materials into equipment without repeatedly moving between rooms.

sections.title: Input, fuel and output
paragraphs: Put the material to process in the upper slot and fuel in the lower slot. The output appears separately after processing. Furnaces handle more than metal: supported recipes include food, building materials and sponge drying. If nothing starts, check the recipe, available fuel and whether the output slot can accept the result before assuming the furnace is broken.

sections.title: Plan a smelting batch
paragraphs: The community reference describes ordinary furnace processing as 200 game ticks per item. Fuel types do not all last equally long, so count the intended batch before spending a valuable fuel source. The visible progress arrow describes the current item; it does not mean every item in the input stack has already finished. Collect and check the output.

sections.title: Recover the block safely
paragraphs: For this Java entry, use a pickaxe when recovering the furnace: breaking it without one does not drop the block. Empty important contents first so you can track what you recovered. Bedrock behavior differs, so do not treat the Java recovery rule or dataset number 335 as a universal rule. The named item is minecraft:furnace.

history.label: 19 February 2010
history.detail: Mojang’s retrospective dates the furnace to version 0.31. It replaced a much less convenient early smelting approach and later gained a more familiar interface and wider uses.

sections.title: The diamond-tool milestone
paragraphs: Use three diamonds across the top row of a crafting table, with two sticks down the middle below them. The result is one diamond pickaxe. For ordinary Survival progression, an iron pickaxe lets you collect diamond ore drops before making this upgrade. Check the output before spending scarce diamonds on a different tool by mistake.

sections.title: What it unlocks
paragraphs: A diamond pickaxe can harvest obsidian, which lower-tier pickaxes do not drop as an item. Netherite can also harvest it, so diamond is not the only valid tier. In practice, plan a safe standing position and an exit before working around obsidian and lava; upgrading the tool does not protect your character from environmental damage.

sections.title: Durability and maintenance
paragraphs: This Java catalog lists 1,561 durability and a maximum stack of one. Read durability as a tool resource, not as damage dealt to a target. An anvil can repair tools using their material or combine compatible tools; repeated anvil work can raise the experience cost. Save your valuable pickaxe before the remaining durability is exhausted.

sections.title: Do not mix tool statistics
paragraphs: The record number 939 identifies this Java 26.1 dataset entry; use minecraft:diamond_pickaxe when discussing the named item. Java and Bedrock combat rules are not interchangeable. Mining speed also depends on the block and conditions, so one speed label cannot describe every task. Mods, server rules and enchantments may change the result seen in a demonstration.

history.label: From diamond to netherite
history.detail: The current community recipe documents a diamond pickaxe as an input for a netherite upgrade, together with a Netherite Upgrade template and a netherite ingot. This is an equipment progression path, not an automatic transformation.
